title: Carbon-13: Natural Abundance and Hyperpolarized
summary: 13C is spin 1/2 at 1.07 percent natural abundance with a gyromagnetic ratio of 10.7084 MHz/T, so a 3T system runs at 32.1 MHz and a 7T at 75.0 MHz, and the receptivity per nucleus in natural material is about 1.7e-4 of 1H, roughly one part in 5900. What you buy for that penalty is a 190 ppm shift range in which almost every carbon position in almost every metabolite is separately resolved, so glycogen C1, the lipid chain carbons, and glutamate C4 versus glutamine C4 are distinct lines rather than an overlapped multiplet. Natural abundance work is therefore hostage to 1H decoupling and NOE, both of which are SAR limited, and to large voxels and long averaging; 13C-labelled substrate infusion buys enrichment and turns the experiment into a flux measurement. Dissolution DNP takes a different route entirely, delivering roughly 30 to 45 percent liquid-state polarization against a thermal 2.5e-6 at 3T, an enhancement near 1e5, but the magnetization is non-renewable and decays with the C1 carbonyl T1, which gives a working window of about 60 s and one shot at getting the setup right.

facts.label: Nucleus properties
facts.value: Spin 1/2, 1.07 percent natural abundance, 10.7084 MHz/T; 32.1 MHz at 3T, 75.0 MHz at 7T. Receptivity per nucleus at natural abundance is 1.70e-4 of 1H, about 1 part in 5900
facts.note: The gamma cubed term alone costs a factor of 63 (0.0159 of 1H at 100 percent enrichment); the remaining factor of 93 is the isotope abundance, which is the only part you can buy back by infusing label.

facts.label: In vivo chemical shift range
facts.value: Roughly 0 to 190 ppm referenced to TMS, from lipid CH3 at 14.1 ppm to carbonyls near 172 to 185 ppm. 200 ppm is 6.4 kHz at 3T and 15.0 kHz at 7T
facts.note: That bandwidth is the reason hard-pulse excitation is uneven across the spectrum and why adiabatic half passage or BIR-4 with a surface coil is standard; it also sets the receiver bandwidth and, for CSI, the spectral sampling.

facts.label: One-bond 1H-13C coupling and decoupling gain
facts.value: 1J(CH) about 125 to 145 Hz for aliphatic CH and CH2, about 170 Hz for the anomeric C1 of glucose and glycogen, about 155 to 160 Hz for olefinic carbons
facts.note: Undecoupled, an anomeric CH is a doublet split by 170 Hz, which at 3T is 5.3 ppm of the 13C scale; collapsing it roughly doubles peak height for a CH and gains more for CH2 and CH3, before any NOE.

facts.label: NOE ceiling
facts.value: Maximum 13C{1H} NOE enhancement is 1 + gamma_H/(2 gamma_C) = 2.99 in the extreme narrowing limit; in vivo enhancements are typically 1.2 to 2.0 and are metabolite specific
facts.note: NOE is what makes natural abundance brain glycogen detectable at all, but because it differs between carbons with different local mobility it is a per-peak correction, not a global scale factor.

facts.label: Glycogen, the natural abundance workhorse
facts.value: C1 resonance at 100.5 ppm. Human liver 200 to 300 mM glucosyl units, and the in vivo 13C signal is essentially 100 percent NMR visible (in vivo to enzymatic ratio 0.95 +/- 0.05). Skeletal muscle roughly 60 to 100 mM; human thigh measured at 64.8 +/- 20.6 mM at 3T. Brain glycogen is only about 3 to 5 mM
facts.note: Liver and muscle glycogen are high enough to see at natural abundance; brain glycogen is not, and needs 13C-labelled glucose infusion plus NOE even at 7T.

facts.label: Lipid carbons
facts.value: Bulk methylene 30.2 ppm, terminal CH3 14.1 ppm, olefinic CH=CH near 130 ppm, diallylic CH2 near 25.6 to 28 ppm, ester carbonyl near 172 ppm, glycerol backbone at 62 and 69 ppm
facts.note: 13C separates saturated, monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fractions by distinct carbons rather than by one crowded 1H olefinic peak, which is the main reason to do hepatic or adipose lipid composition by 13C instead of 1H.

facts.label: 13C-labelled substrate infusion
facts.value: [1-13C]glucose at 99 percent enrichment, given as a priming bolus then a variable-rate infusion over 90 to 120 min to hold plasma glucose near 8 to 12 mM and plasma enrichment near 30 to 70 percent. [2-13C]acetate is the glial alternative. Key readouts: glutamate C4 at 34.2 ppm and glutamine C4 at 31.7 ppm, separated by 2.5 ppm, which is 80 Hz at 3T and 187 Hz at 7T
facts.note: Label from [1-13C]glucose reaches glutamate C4 through pyruvate and acetyl-CoA; acetate is taken up preferentially by astrocytes, so [2-13C]acetate labels the glial TCA pool first and is how the neuronal and glial compartments are separated.

facts.label: Human brain fluxes from 13C turnover curves
facts.value: Neuronal TCA cycle flux in occipital gray matter reported over roughly 0.5 to 0.9 umol per g per min, glutamate to glutamine cycling flux Vcyc roughly 0.3 to 0.5 umol per g per min; higher VTCA values above 1 umol per g per min have also been published. Vcyc/(0.5 x VTCAn) is near 0.75 to 1.0
facts.note: This is a genuine range, not a measurement spread: the numbers depend on the metabolic model, the assumed compartment sizes and whether dilution from unlabelled substrate is fitted, so quote the model with the flux.

facts.label: Dissolution DNP conditions
facts.value: Neat [1-13C]pyruvic acid doped with about 15 mM trityl radical AH111501, polarized at 5 T and 0.8 K with 139.87 GHz microwaves in a clinical SPINlab; build-up to plateau takes about 3 h. Earlier preclinical systems used 3.35 T, 1.4 K and about 94 GHz
facts.note: The build-up time, not the scan, is what sets the throughput of a hyperpolarized study; one polarizer channel is one dose every few hours unless the system holds several samples.

facts.label: What the enhancement actually is
facts.value: Thermal 13C polarization at 3T and 37 C is 2.5e-6. Clinical liquid-state polarization at quality control is roughly 30 to 45 percent, an enhancement near 1.2e5 to 1.8e5, and the community shorthand of more than 10,000-fold is a conservative floor
facts.note: Five orders of magnitude in polarization does not become five orders in image SNR: the delivered agent is only a few mM in tissue, the magnetization is spent by the RF and by T1, and you get one pass with no averaging.

facts.label: T1 of the C1 carbonyl
facts.value: About 60 to 70 s in aqueous buffer at 3T; roughly 20 to 45 s in blood and in vivo. Carbonyl relaxation is dominated by chemical shift anisotropy, whose rate scales as B0 squared, so T1 falls as field rises
facts.note: This is one of the reasons hyperpolarized 13C has stayed at 3T; a higher field buys spectral separation but shortens the carbonyl T1 and does not increase the signal, which comes from the polarizer rather than from B0.

facts.label: Human dose and injection
facts.value: 0.43 +/- 0.05 mL/kg of a 250 mM solution, about 0.1 mmol/kg, so roughly 30 mL and 7.5 mmol for a 70 kg adult; injected at 5 mL/s followed by a 20 mL saline flush at 5 mL/s. Blood pyruvate rises from a baseline of 0.06 to 0.145 mM to a peak near 1.4 mM
facts.note: 0.43 mL/kg is the top of the Phase 1 dose escalation, not a tracer dose: it raises circulating pyruvate roughly tenfold to twentyfold, so this is a bolus metabolic challenge and should be reported as one.

facts.label: The working window
facts.value: Dynamic acquisition starts at or just after the end of injection and runs 60 to 90 s with 2 to 5 s temporal resolution. Bolus arrival in the prostate varies by +/- 10 s between patients
facts.note: Because arrival time varies more than a single time point can tolerate, essentially every current human study acquires dynamically rather than at one summed time point; a fixed-delay single shot will sometimes miss the bolus entirely.

facts.label: The metabolic readout
facts.value: Normal human brain at 3T: kPL = 0.012 +/- 0.006 per s for pyruvate to lactate, kPB = 0.002 +/- 0.002 per s for pyruvate to bicarbonate. Prostate cancer bone metastases: kPL = 0.020 +/- 0.006 per s, liver metastases 0.026 per s
facts.note: kPB is about a sixth of kPL, which is why bicarbonate, the only in vivo readout of pyruvate dehydrogenase flux and the one that matters most in heart studies, is the hardest peak to detect and the first to be lost to spectral leakage from lactate.

practice: Set the 13C centre frequency from the measured 1H water frequency using the gyromagnetic ratio and the known chemical shift offsets rather than from a 13C prescan; the consensus group preferred this 23/24. Shim on the 1H signal with conventional auto-shim, then switch nuclei.

Expect no 13C body coil. Clinical scanners have none, so transmit is from an in-bore local coil with far worse B1 uniformity than the 1H body coil, and flip angle error propagates straight into AUC ratios and into kPL. Acquire a B1 map, or use a real-time Bloch-Siegert measurement after injection, and use dual-tuned 1H/13C coils for brain and prostate so nothing has to be swapped between scans.

Use small, constant-through-time flip angles for hyperpolarized dynamics. Variable flip angle schemes that promise to spend magnetization optimally are highly sensitive to bolus timing and to B1 error, and in a multi-centre setting that sensitivity is a reproducibility problem rather than an SNR gain.
Inject any gadolinium contrast after the 13C acquisition, never before. Gadolinium shortens the hyperpolarized agent relaxation and there is no way to recover the lost magnetization.

Budget SAR and TR together for natural abundance work. The 1H decoupling train is the dominant SAR term, not the 13C excitation, and it is what forbids the short TR you wanted for averaging. Low-power or stochastic decoupling schemes at 3T exist precisely to break that deadlock; WALTZ-16 and adiabatic WURST cost more.

Rehearse the dissolution, quality control and injection chain on the clock. Polarization decays with T1 from the moment of dissolution, so a 30 s delay at the QC bench is a fixed percentage of the dose gone, and no amount of good scanning afterwards recovers it.

For absolute glycogen or lipid quantification, reference to an external 13C standard of known concentration measured in the same coil geometry and loading, and correct each peak with its own T1 and its own NOE factor. Coil loading changes between a liver and a calf and so does the sensitive volume.

Record the agent parameters as data, not as pharmacy paperwork: pyruvate concentration, residual electron paramagnetic agent, pH, temperature, dose volume and polarization. The consensus group made the first five mandatory to report; polarization did not reach consensus as mandatory only because current measurement methods are not trusted, not because it does not matter.
pitfalls: Hyperpolarized magnetization is non-renewable and unaveraged. Every RF pulse spends part of it and it never comes back, so a wrong centre frequency, a bad shim, a mistimed trigger or a coil that was not plugged in costs the entire study and a whole polarizer cycle. Everything that can be checked on a thermal phantom must be checked before the dissolution starts.

The lactate-to-pyruvate ratio is not a flux. It depends on delivery and perfusion, on the flip angle actually delivered, on when you started sampling relative to the bolus, and on the size of the endogenous lactate pool the label is exchanging into. Two sites running different flip angle schemes will report different ratios from identical physiology, which is exactly why AUC ratios and normalized AUCs, with a harmonized pipeline, are the preferred multi-centre metrics.

Bicarbonate is where the oxidative information is and it is the peak you are most likely to lose. With kPB around a sixth of kPL, the bicarbonate signal sits close to the noise, and in metabolite-specific imaging spectral leakage from the very large lactate resonance can fill the bicarbonate channel with something that is not bicarbonate.

Subcutaneous and bone-marrow lipid dominates a natural abundance 13C spectrum acquired with a surface coil. Signal from outside the nominal voxel rides in through the coil sensitivity profile and buries the 20 to 60 ppm region where the metabolites are, so localization and outer-volume suppression are load-bearing, not optional refinements.

A single NOE factor and a single T1 applied across a natural abundance spectrum biases every relative concentration in it. Both are per-carbon and both change with field, so a correction table imported from a 1.5T liver paper does not transfer to a 7T calf study.

1H decoupling at 3T and above is SAR limited rather than hardware limited, and the limit is the head or body average over the whole sequence. A decoupling duty cycle chosen to maximise linewidth collapse will often force a TR long enough that the SNR you gained per shot is lost again in the shots you cannot take.
